children: SpaceX's Falcon 9 rocket lifts off at Cape Canaveral, Fla. on October 1, 2026.
SpaceX is reportedly in discussions with banks and investment management firms to borrow $40 billion to purchase chips from Nvidia.

The company headed by Elon Musk is aiming to raise approximately $10 billion in bank loans and an additional $30 billion in investment-grade debt to pay for the chips, according to people familiar with the matter who spoke to the Financial Times.
That $40 billion would represent basically all of the company's projected $44.5 billion in revenue this year, according to FactSet.

The New York-headquartered Apollo Global Management is anticipated to lead the deal, which is expected to close in 2027, the people said. They added that bond-fund giant Pimco is one of the firms in talks about funding the deal.
Shares in SpaceX (SPCX) declined almost 2% to $169.15 in premarket trading, while Nvidia's stock (NVDA) edged 0.2% higher.
SpaceX, Nvidia, Pimco and Apollo did not immediately respond to MarketWatch's requests for comment.
Less than two weeks ago, Musk said his artificial-intelligence start-up xAI would aim to more than double its amount of Nvidia chips at its Colossus 2 data center by the end of the year.

He wrote in a post on X that the facility currently has 110,000 Nvidia GB200 chips and 440,000 GB300 chips. However, he said the company behind the Grok AI chatbot was expecting to have another 220,000 GB300s operational by the following week and an additional 220,000 units in November. Musk added yet another 220,000 may come online in December "if we get lucky."
The latest reported move comes as Musk's companies seek to accelerate in the race against technology competitors to dominate in the AI industry.

In August, Nvidia said it was partnering with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR to create a $500 billion funding platform to help develop third-party capital pools at "attractive rates" for customers of the chip-designing giant to finance the buildout of AI.
